gloss: to distract; to divert; to dispel

definitions.gloss: to distract; to divert; to dispel
definitions.explanation: to take one's mind off something unpleasant by focusing on something else

examples.japanese: {寂|さび}しさを{紛|まぎ}らわす。
{退屈|たいくつ}を{紛|まぎ}らわすために{本|ほん}を{読|よ}む。
examples.english: I read books to dispel boredom.

examples.japanese: {仕事|しごと}に{没頭|ぼっとう}して{悲|かな}しみを{紛|まぎ}らわせた。
examples.english: I immersed myself in work to distract myself from grief.

notes:
USAGE:
- を{紛|まぎ}らわす (to distract from, to dispel)
- {寂|さび}しさを{紛|まぎ}らわす (to distract from loneliness)
- {退屈|たいくつ}を{紛|まぎ}らわす (to kill boredom)
- {悲|かな}しみを{紛|まぎ}らわす (to distract from sadness)

NUANCE:
Implies coping with negative feelings by redirecting attention. The underlying problem isn't solved, just temporarily set aside.

TRANSITIVITY:
Transitive ({他動詞|たどうし})

RELATED:
- {紛|まぎ}れる (to be distracted - intransitive)
- {紛|まぎ}らわしい (confusing, misleading)
- {気|き}を{紛|まぎ}らわす (to distract oneself)
